title: Program.Workflow — the workflow document
description: A workflow governs the lifecycle of a thing: its states, the transitions between them, who may make each, and what each requires. It does not describe how work is done — a procedure does that. The join between the two layers is here (state.onEnter.startProcedure, transition.requires.procedure) and in the procedure's step.advances. Stored whole in config.DefinitionVersion.PayloadText. See docs/design/PROCEDURE-ENGINE.md.

cancellation.description: A terminal state reached by abandoning the subject rather than completing it.

roles.description: security.Role codes permitted to act on the subject while in this state. Empty: read-only.

onEnter.description: Effects when the subject enters this state. The workflow-to-procedure direction of the join (FR-2.1).

name.description: The verb on the button, and what a procedure step's advances.transition cites.

roles.description: Who may make this transition. Default: the from-state's roles.

signoff.description: A segregation action name, when this transition is an attested act.

requires.description: Guards. All must hold. A guard that is Unknown blocks the transition and says which facts were unknown.

startProcedure.description: Program.Procedure key. Starts an instance over this workflow's subject, pinned to the procedure's approved version at that instant.

oneOf.description: Satisfied when a procedure instance started from this workflow instance has completed with the named outcome.
A grammar-1 boolean over the subject's facts — an AST node under "when", as FORMULA-GRAMMAR.md §7 prescribes.
